title: Explicit conjugacy of the two scalar-counit maps across site comparisons
statement:
Let $\mathcal X_R,\mathcal Y_R,\mathcal X'_R,\mathcal Y'_R$ for $R=A,B$ be categories [def-nagata-category]. All functors preserve identities and composition; all transformations below are natural, and composition is right to left with the canonical functor associators. Give functors $F_R:\mathcal X_R\to\mathcal Y_R$, $H_R:\mathcal Y_R\to\mathcal X_R$, $F'_R:\mathcal X'_R\to\mathcal Y'_R$, $H'_R:\mathcal Y'_R\to\mathcal X'_R$, and natural maps $\epsilon_R:F_RH_R\to1$, $\epsilon'_R:F'_RH'_R\to1$; these maps need not be counits of adjunctions. Give comparison functors $C_{X,R}:\mathcal X_R\to\mathcal X'_R$, $C_{Y,R}:\mathcal Y_R\to\mathcal Y'_R$, with $C_{Y,A}$ essentially surjective (every target object is isomorphic to one of its values). Give natural isomorphisms
$$c_R:C_{Y,R}F_R\xrightarrow{\sim}F'_RC_{X,R},\qquad r_R:H'_RC_{Y,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{X,R}H_R$$
such that for every $L\in\mathcal Y_R$,
$$\epsilon'_{R,C_{Y,R}L}=C_{Y,R}(\epsilon_{R,L})\circ c_R(H_RL)^{-1}\circ F'_R(r_{R,L}).$$
Give functors $T_X:\mathcal X_A\to\mathcal X_B$, $T_Y:\mathcal Y_A\to\mathcal Y_B$, $T'_X:\mathcal X'_A\to\mathcal X'_B$, $T'_Y:\mathcal Y'_A\to\mathcal Y'_B$ and natural isomorphisms
$$\delta_X:T'_XC_{X,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{X,B}T_X,\qquad \delta_Y:T'_YC_{Y,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{Y,B}T_Y.$$
Give natural maps $q:T_YF_A\to F_BT_X$, $q':T'_YF'_A\to F'_BT'_X$, $a:T_XH_A\to H_BT_Y$, $a':T'_XH'_A\to H'_BT'_Y$. Assume the two specified comparison squares, for all $M\in\mathcal X_A$ and $L\in\mathcal Y_A$:
$$F'_B(\delta_{X,M})q'_{C_{X,A}M}T'_Y(c_A(M))
=c_B(T_XM)C_{Y,B}(q_M)\delta_{Y,F_AM},$$
$$r_{B,T_YL}H'_B(\delta_{Y,L})a'_{C_{Y,A}L}
=C_{X,B}(a_L)\delta_{X,H_AL}T'_X(r_{A,L}).$$
Define the parallel pairs
$$D_L=\epsilon_{B,T_YL}F_B(a_L)q_{H_AL},\quad E_L=T_Y(\epsilon_{A,L}),$$
$$D'_K=\epsilon'_{B,T'_YK}F'_B(a'_K)q'_{H'_AK},\quad E'_K=T'_Y(\epsilon'_{A,K}).$$
Set the isomorphism
$$Z_L=\delta_{Y,F_AH_AL}\circ T'_Y(c_A(H_AL)^{-1})\circ T'_Y(F'_A(r_{A,L})).$$
Then the following two identities hold separately, without assuming $D_L=E_L$:
$$\delta_{Y,L}D'_{C_{Y,A}L}=C_{Y,B}(D_L)Z_L,\qquad
\delta_{Y,L}E'_{C_{Y,A}L}=C_{Y,B}(E_L)Z_L.$$
Consequently, if $D_L=E_L$ for every $L\in\mathcal Y_A$, then $D'_K=E'_K$ for every $K\in\mathcal Y'_A$. No full faithfulness, invertibility of $q,q',a,a'$, adjunction axioms, or identification of a comparison isomorphism with an identity is assumed.

proof.text:
Fix $L\in\mathcal Y_A$ and abbreviate $M=H_AL$, $C=C_{Y,A}$, $V=C_{Y,B}$, $s=r_{A,L}:H'_ACL\to C_{X,A}M$, and $u=\delta_{Y,L}:T'_YCL\to VT_YL$. Composition remains right to left. By [def-nagata-category] we may reassociate composites. Naturality here means $Q(h)\alpha_U=\alpha_WP(h)$ for $\alpha:P\to Q$ and $h:U\to W$. Thus naturality of $\epsilon'_B$ at $u$ and the stipulated evaluation formula at $T_YL$ give
$$uD'_{CL}=V(\epsilon_{B,T_YL})c_B(H_BT_YL)^{-1}F'_B\bigl(r_{B,T_YL}H'_B(u)a'_{CL}\bigr)q'_{H'_ACL}.$$
The full composite has the same source $T'_YF'_AH'_ACL$ and target $VT_YL$ as the left side; the factors inside $F'_B$ compose from $T'_XH'_ACL$ to $C_{X,B}H_BT_YL$.

source.place: Charts, actual scalar-counit transport: explicit categorical calculation, step 1

proof.text:
Substitute exactly the assumed right comparison square, whose argument is this $L$, into the parenthesized composite of Step 1. Functoriality of $F'_B$ then gives
$$uD'_{CL}=V(\epsilon_{B,T_YL})c_B(H_BT_YL)^{-1}F'_B(C_{X,B}(a_L))F'_B(\delta_{X,M})F'_B(T'_X(s))q'_{H'_ACL}.$$
This substitution uses no inverse of $a_L$ or $a'_{CL}$.

source.place: Charts, actual scalar-counit transport: explicit categorical calculation, step 2

proof.text:
Naturality of $c_B$ at $a_L:T_XM\to H_BT_YL$, followed by composition with the inverses of its two isomorphism components, gives
$$c_B(H_BT_YL)^{-1}F'_B(C_{X,B}(a_L))=V(F_B(a_L))c_B(T_XM)^{-1}.$$
Naturality of $q'$ at $s:H'_ACL\to C_{X,A}M$ gives
$$F'_B(T'_X(s))q'_{H'_ACL}=q'_{C_{X,A}M}T'_Y(F'_A(s)).$$
Use these two equations in Step 2. Neither equation cancels $q'$ or $a$.

source.place: Charts, actual scalar-counit transport: explicit categorical calculation, step 3

proof.text:
The assumed left comparison square at $M$ can be composed on the left with $c_B(T_XM)^{-1}$ and on the right with $T'_Y(c_A(M)^{-1})$, giving
$$c_B(T_XM)^{-1}F'_B(\delta_{X,M})q'_{C_{X,A}M}=V(q_M)\delta_{Y,F_AM}T'_Y(c_A(M)^{-1}).$$
Substitution into Step 3, and combining the three successive $V$-images using preservation of composition, yields
$$uD'_{CL}=V(\epsilon_{B,T_YL}F_B(a_L)q_M)\delta_{Y,F_AM}T'_Y(c_A(M)^{-1})T'_Y(F'_A(s))=V(D_L)Z_L.$$
This proves the first identity without any equality hypothesis on $D_L,E_L$.

source.place: Charts, actual scalar-counit transport: explicit categorical calculation, step 4

proof.text:
Independently, use the stipulated evaluation formula for $R=A$ and preservation of composition by $T'_Y$:
$$uE'_{CL}=uT'_Y(C(\epsilon_{A,L}))T'_Y(c_A(M)^{-1})T'_Y(F'_A(s)).$$
Naturality of $\delta_Y$ at $\epsilon_{A,L}:F_AM\to L$ says
$$uT'_Y(C(\epsilon_{A,L}))=V(T_Y(\epsilon_{A,L}))\delta_{Y,F_AM}.$$
Substituting proves $uE'_{CL}=V(E_L)Z_L$, the second identity. This argument does not use the first identity or assume $D_L=E_L$.

source.place: Charts, actual scalar-counit transport: explicit categorical calculation, step 5

proof.text: Now assume $D_L=E_L$ for all $L$. Steps 4 and 5 give $uD'_{CL}=uE'_{CL}$. Compose on the left with $u^{-1}$ to obtain $D'_{CL}=E'_{CL}$. Here only $u=\delta_{Y,L}$ is cancelled; no faithfulness of $V$ is needed. For arbitrary $K\in\mathcal Y'_A$, essential surjectivity as explicitly assumed provides $L$ and an isomorphism $t:CL\xrightarrow{\sim}K$.

source.place: Charts, actual scalar-counit transport: explicit categorical calculation, step 6

proof.text:
Put $P=T'_YF'_AH'_A$. To spell out the naturality needed for this $t$, write $h=H'_A(t)$. Naturality of $q',a',\epsilon'_B$, in that order, gives
$$q'_{H'_AK}T'_Y(F'_A(h))=F'_B(T'_X(h))q'_{H'_ACL},$$
$$a'_KT'_X(h)=H'_B(T'_Y(t))a'_{CL},\qquad \epsilon'_{B,T'_YK}F'_B(H'_B(T'_Y(t)))=T'_Y(t)\epsilon'_{B,T'_YCL}.$$
Compose these three equations to get $D'_KP(t)=T'_Y(t)D'_{CL}$. Naturality of $\epsilon'_A$ at $t$, mapped by $T'_Y$, gives $E'_KP(t)=T'_Y(t)E'_{CL}$. Step 6 identifies the two right sides. The inverse of $P(t)$ is $P(t^{-1})$, since $P$ preserves composition and identities. Compose on the right with this inverse to deduce $D'_K=E'_K$.

Step 1: naturality of eps'_B at delta_{Y,L} plus the B evaluation formula; def-nagata-category is used only for associativity. Step 2: the right square. Step 3: naturality of c_B at a_L and of q' at r_{A,L}. Step 4: the left square conjugated by c_B^{-1} and T'_Y(c_A^{-1}), giving V(D_L)Z_L. Step 5: naturality of delta_Y at eps_{A,L}, independent of Step 4. Step 6: cancel delta_{Y,L} and use the explicit essential-surjectivity hypothesis. Step 7: naturality of q', a', eps'_B and eps'_A at t, with P(t)^{-1}=P(t^{-1}). Every step checks, and every step is genuinely elementary. Only c_A, c_B, delta_Y and t are inverted; q, q', a, a' and eps are never inverted, and C_{Y,B} is never assumed faithful. Edge cases: identity comparisons, an empty Y_A (essential surjectivity forces Y'_A empty), and zero evaluations in additive categories. The only citer, lem-sp-chart-counit-scalar-transport, takes exactly the two identities and the all-K consequence, and the statement gives both.
